test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The WHO has found that young adolescents (ages 10-14) face a higher risk of complications and death as a result of pregnancy than other women. What is the most likely reason for higher MMR (maternal mortality rate) in young women?

options.text: Their body size is often too small to deliver a baby
They are the group with the highest pregnancy rate
Their bodies do not support a foetus formation
They are ignorant or negligent about health guidelines

solution:
The correct answer is __**Their body size is often too small to deliver a baby**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most likely reason for higher maternal mortality rates (MMR) in young women (ages 10-14) is **their body size is often too small to deliver a baby**.
 
• **At this age, the body may not be fully developed for pregnancy and childbirth,** 
 
• It **can lead to complications such as obstructed labour**, high blood pressure, and other serious health risks.
 
• **Young adolescents may also face additional challenges** in terms of prenatal care and support during labour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry for Women and Child Development (WCD) has set up a task force to look into factors that affect the Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) among Indian women.
 
• The task force will be headed by Jaya Jaitly and it will submit its report by 31st July of next month.
 
• The task Force will examine the issues related to Infant Mortality Rate, Maternal Mortality Rate, Total Fertility Rate, Sex Ratio at Birth, Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and any other issues pertaining to health and nutrition.
 
• It will also suggest measures for promoting higher education among women.
 
• Union Finance Minister, Nirmala Sitharaman in her Budget Speech for 2020-21 has announced to set up a task force for women.
 
• Ministry of Women and Child Development: Smriti Irani
